record.original_question: For each real s>0, does there exist an integer m>=1 such that the entire function sum_{k>=0} k^s x^k/(k!)^m belongs to L-P+, the Laguerre-Polya class of real entire functions with nonnegative Taylor coefficients?

evidence.quote: Problem 40. Is it true that for every s in R^+, there exists an m in N, such that sum_{k=0}^infinity k^s x^k/(k!)^m belongs to L - P+.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Laguerre–Pólya class L–P consists of entire functions f that are locally uniform limits of sequences of real polynomials all of whose zeros are real. Equivalently, f ∈ L–P if and only if it admits a Hadamard-type representation
  f(x) = c x^n e^{-α x^2 + β x} ∏_{k} (1 - x/x_k) e^{x/x_k},
with c, β, x_k ∈ ℝ, α ≥ 0, n ∈ ℤ_{≥0}, and ∑ 1/x_k^2 < ∞. Let L–P^+ denote the subclass of those f ∈ L–P whose Taylor coefficients at 0 are all nonnegative real numbers (equivalently, all zeros of f are real and nonpositive).

Question: For every real number s > 0, does there exist a positive integer m such that the entire function
  F_{s,m}(x) := ∑_{k=0}^{∞} k^s · x^k / (k!)^m
belongs to L–P^+ ?

The general literature on L–P and Turán-type inequalities discusses related families but no source confirms a proof or disproof of this statement.
